definition: The Standard and Poor’s 500 (S&P 500) is a stock market index that tracks the performance of 500 of the largest publicly traded U.S. companies, ranked by market capitalization. The S&P 500 reflects the overall movement of the stock prices of these companies and is widely used to measure the performance of large-cap U.S. stocks and the broader economy.
